title: USBGuard integration
line: With USBGuard running, USB devices plugged in while the screen is locked are now blocked, and you get a notification about them after unlocking.
explanation: Plasma had no USBGuard integration at all: a device plugged into a locked machine was handled exactly as if the user were there, so the lock screen gave no protection against evil-maid style USB attacks, which is the part of the wish GNOME already covers and the one the last comment asks for. The screen locker now sets USBGuard's InsertedDevicePolicy from apply-policy to block while locked and back on unlock, leaving it alone if the admin set something else. A keyboard is still let in when no other keyboard is connected, internal (hardwired) devices that reappear after resume are allowed, the rest stay blocked and a notification after unlock says to reconnect them; Screen Locking settings get a "Block new USB devices while locked" checkbox (on by default) shown only when USBGuard is installed.

commits.message:
Block new USB devices while the screen is locked with USBGuard

When USBGuard is running, anything plugged in while the screen is locked
is accepted, so locking doesn't protect against malicious USB devices.
New devices are now blocked until unlock, with a setting and a notice.

BUG: 454479

media.caption: Today: a USB stick plugged in while the screen is locked is allowed by USBGuard.
With the change: while locked the stick and a second keyboard are blocked, the internal webcam reappearing is allowed, and the policy is restored on unlock.
New "Block new USB devices while locked" checkbox, shown only when USBGuard is installed.
Notification after unlocking when a device was blocked.
